source_quote: Working breed groups maintained elevated hip dysplasia prevalence across North American screening registries.
Cumulative mechanical load increased osteoarthritis prevalence in working dog populations over career length.
Sporting breeds showed persistent otitis externa burden linked to water exposure and pendulous ear conformation.
Atopic dermatitis prevalence remained moderate in sporting breed dermatology surveillance programs.
Deep-chested hound lines showed increased gastric dilatation-volvulus prevalence in emergency referral data.
Hound breeds with elongated spinal morphology carried elevated intervertebral disc disease risk.
Terrier breed groups demonstrated increased chronic inflammatory dermatitis prevalence across surveillance data.
Companion toy and small breeds carried the highest periodontal disease prevalence in primary-care populations.
Herding lineages showed above-baseline idiopathic epilepsy prevalence in neurology referral cohorts.
Toy function group retained the highest luxating patella prevalence across orthopedic screening populations.
